notes: Year 9 Fundamentals; 3 key concepts + H2O(l)/(s)/(g) examples
body_text_excerpt: Chem Games Profile Leaderboards Games Cheat Sheets Log in / Register Back to Cheat Sheets Year 9 Fundamentals States of Matter Particle arrangement, energy levels, and phase changes in solids, liquids, and gases. Key Concepts Solids have fixed volume and shape with tightly packed particles. Liquids take the shape of their container but maintain fixed volume. Gases expand to fill any container with high particle movement. Example Formulas & Reactions Water (Liquid) H 2 O (l) Ice (Solid) H 2 O (s) Steam (Gas) H 2 O (g) ChemGames — Making chemistry visual, playful, and intuitive. © 2026 ChemGames. All rights reserved. body_text_excerpt: Chem Games Profile Leaderboards Games Cheat Sheets Log in / Register Back to Cheat Sheets Year 9 Acids & Bases Acids & Bases Understanding the pH scale, proton donors (acids), and hydroxide release (bases). Key Concepts Acids have pH < 7 and release Hydrogen ions (H+). Bases have pH > 7 and release Hydroxide ions (OH-). Neutral substances (pure water) sit at pH 7. title: Balancing Chemical Equations Cheat Sheet | ChemGames
meta_description: Applying the Law of Conservation of Mass so atom counts match on both sides.
notes: Year 10 Equations; coefficients not subscripts; H2+O2->H2O
body_text_excerpt: Chem Games Profile Leaderboards Games Cheat Sheets Log in / Register Back to Cheat Sheets Year 10 Equations Balancing Chemical Equations Applying the Law of Conservation of Mass so atom counts match on both sides. Key Concepts Matter cannot be created or destroyed in a chemical reaction. Adjust coefficients (big numbers in front), NEVER subscripts. Count atoms of each element on Reactant side vs. Product side. Example Formulas & Reactions Unbalanced H 2 + O 2 → H 2 O Balanced 2 H 2 + O 2 → 2 H 2 O ChemGames — Making chemistry visual, playful, and intuitive. © 2026 ChemGames. All rights reserved. Feedback

title: Chemical Bonds & Structure Cheat Sheet | ChemGames
meta_description: Understanding how atoms share or transfer electrons to form stable compounds.
chemistry_topic: Ionic vs covalent bonding, valence electrons
notes: Year 9 Fundamentals; CO2 covalent, NaCl ionic
body_text_excerpt: Chem Games Profile Leaderboards Games Cheat Sheets Log in / Register Back to Cheat Sheets Year 9 Fundamentals Chemical Bonds & Structure Understanding how atoms share or transfer electrons to form stable compounds. Key Concepts Covalent Bonds: Non-metals share electrons to achieve a full outer shell. Ionic Bonds: Metals transfer electrons to non-metals, creating oppositely charged ions. Valence electrons determine an element’s reactivity and bonding capacity. Example Formulas & Reactions Covalent Compound C O 2 ( Ca r b o n Di o x i d e ) Ionic Compound Na Cl ( So d i u m Ch l o r i d e ) ChemGames — Making chemistry visual, playful, and intuitive. © 2026 ChemGames. title: Writing Chemical Formulas Cheat Sheet | ChemGames
meta_description: Translating chemical names into standardized symbolic formulas.
body_text_excerpt: Chem Games Profile Leaderboards Games Cheat Sheets Log in / Register Back to Cheat Sheets Year 10 Equations Writing Chemical Formulas Translating chemical names into standardized symbolic formulas. Key Concepts The symbol of the metal (cation) is always written before the non-metal (anion). Use subscripts to indicate the number of atoms (e.g., the 2 in H2O). Polyatomic ions act as a single unit and need brackets if there is more than one (e.g., Ca(OH)2). Example Formulas & Reactions Calcium Carbonate Ca C O 3 Aluminium Oxide Al 2 O 3 ChemGames — Making chemistry visual, playful, and intuitive. © 2026 ChemGames. All rights reserved. Feedback
